title: Choose the look for Veil
question: The roll assigned the carbonless two-part form. Keep it, take another card, or re-roll.

options.label: Carbonless Two-Part Form
options.thesis: Every document becomes a two-part form: your top copy keeps the values, the AI's copy never received them.
options.viewport: Your document on white beside the AI's canary copy, where personal fields arrive as hatched blocks with blue placeholders.
options.risk: Reads as office stationery if paper colour spreads beyond the two copies.

raised.raise: Hatch density is a measured state: solid for the rule layer, hatched for the model.
Placeholders read as codes; hovering one decodes it locally, never on the AI's copy.
The two copies mirror line for line, so every hidden value sits level with its source.
One document owns the workspace; the next sample is one click away.
An honest toggle between the original and exactly what was sent.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Personal data as a network map: every type its own line, every repeat an interchange.
options.viewport: A line strip across the top where each data type runs as one colour, over the page and the AI's text.
options.case: Holds on clarity with a strict colour per type; loses on identification, since a dark mural ground fights long contracts.
options.risk: A dark ground tires the eye on twenty-page leases.

options.label: Security-Tint Envelope
options.thesis: Veil as the security envelope: personal values show only through your own window.
options.viewport: The page with values under tinted lattice, the AI's text as the letter inside, a rail of documents on the left.
options.risk: Also the privacy metaphor most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Every region carries a measured hatch and a stop-delta.
options.viewport: Stacked translucent sheets over an eleven-step ramp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: letting agents and tenants do not think in exposure zones.
options.risk: Reads as a photographer's tool, not a privacy check.
options.kept: Hatch density as a measured state, never decoration.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Names replaced by codes that only the holder can read.
options.viewport: A black field with one coded strip per document.
options.case: Fits the placeholder idea, but an unlabelled black void fails first-time users.
options.risk: Mystery where the task needs plain labels.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: A mirrored score read upward along a centre staff.
options.viewport: Two columns flanking one centre line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: symbol shapes as data are unreadable to this audience.
options.risk: Obscure notation on a tool that must be obvious.
options.kept: Bilateral symmetry as a layout law.

options.label: Vertical Video Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the whole frame, the next one snap away.
options.viewport: One document page full bleed with a glyph rail.
options.case: One document at a time fits, but a swipe feed hides the side-by-side check the task needs.
options.risk: Entertainment cues on a confidentiality tool.

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Coarse pixel letterforms at poster scale.
options.viewport: A pixel headline over dense justified columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: pixel display type reads as a design statement, not a trustworthy tool.
options.kept: An honest toggle between two renderings.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A white two-pane editor with a green accent, type chips and a chat box.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Quillbot and every redaction demo by design.
